summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 7.7% YoY to INR1,344.55 mn, but EBITDA margin slipped to 5.8% and management guides 10-12% FY27 EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR1,344.55 mn, up 7.7% YoY, with gross margin up to 57.5% from 50.5%. EBITDA rose only 1.6% to INR77.79 mn, and margin eased to 5.8% from 6.1%, which management attributed to forex losses on the Mexican peso. H1 was weak because Q1 execution was delayed by GCC supply-chain disruption, with shipments from the UAE stuck by sea. Management expects a low double-digit EBITDA margin in FY27 and targets 20-25% growth, with 14-16% margins over 3-5 years.

segments.name: Sales & projects (S&P)
segments.commentary: Project business is lumpy and carries over 60% of revenue; short-cycle orders of INR5-15 crore are executed quickly, while large orders above INR50 crore run over longer cycles (e.g., INR126 crore steel order over 14-18 months).

segments.name: O&M and spares & consumables
segments.commentary: Around 40% of revenue, described as steady; O&M blended EBITDA margin in the low 20s%. Management reported only the 12-month forward O&M order number. Q1 analyst figure of about INR57 crore O&M executed was not disputed in the call.

segments.name: Sharjah (membranes)
segments.commentary: Utilisation at 50-60%; all membrane products are made in Sharjah and exported, while assembly of export projects has moved to India.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 15-20%, with most of the order book executable in FY27; H2 must deliver about INR422 crore to reach 15% growth, per analyst math.
FY27 EBITDA margin in the low double digits, about 10-12%; management says overall profitability stays single-digit for another year.
FY27 gross margin and EBITDA margin expected to be stable; improvement from FY28.
FY28 target of 14-16% EBITDA margin, with 14-15% described as achievable over the next 3-5 years.
Medium-term growth target of 20-25% per annum, described as a multi-year average given lumpiness.
Order intake of INR500-600 crore expected over the next 6 months from an active pipeline of about INR3,000 crore at a 15-20% conversion rate.
FY27 capex of about INR30-35 crore (Vasai about INR15 crore plus maintenance INR15-20 crore); FY28 capex of INR50-60 crore including Sharjah and a possible alternative unit.
Working capital cycle of 140-150 days; debtor days 110-120; management expects it to stabilise by end-Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Vasai facility: about INR15 crore investment this year, mainly debottlenecking, funded from IPO proceeds; capacity enhancement planned in the next 1-2 years.
Sharjah: scaled back new facility investment; review scale-up decisions in Q4 FY27 once the geopolitical situation stabilises.
FY28 capex planned at INR50-60 crore, including Sharjah start-up and a possible second manufacturing unit planned 4-5 years out.
demand_pricing: Domestic order inflows in H1 FY27 rose 55% YoY; a significant order came from a leading global alco-bev player for a Mexico plant.
Rochem subsidiary won INR14.25 crore solar PV module order (Hyderabad) on 1 Oct 2026, with delivery end-Nov/early Dec and completion by mid-Jan 2027.
Dehumidification (WaHa partnership) and CBG are moving into bidding; management plans INR500-700 crore of bids in the next quarter.
Data centres: no order yet; the company is working on combined dehumidification and water solutions.
Middle East tertiary sewage demonstration project expected to convert to orders in Q3.
Management claims pricing premium on industrial membranes versus Chinese products, citing longevity and value-add; no pricing figures given.

qa_highlights.question: Why are quarterly revenue and margins so volatile over the last eight quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Prerak Goel said the business is H2-heavy, with Q3 and Q4 the strongest quarters, and large project orders cause lumpiness; O&M and spares are steady while S&P project revenue is volatile.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 revenue reach 15-20% growth given H1 de-growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said large steel-sector orders are due for Q4 delivery, work is already under way, and Q3/Q4 execution should meet the growth target.

qa_highlights.question: Why are EBITDA margins in single digits versus peers at 12-16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed costs rose from investments in capacity and new business lines, so operating leverage should lift margins; FY27 EBITDA is guided to low double digits, with 14-16% targeted for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sharjah utilisation and the outlook for the Middle East?
qa_highlights.answer: Sharjah runs at 50-60% utilisation; non-core work was moved to India, and membrane production continues. Shipments by sea from UAE remain uncertain while air freight is normal.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY28 growth and FY27 capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-25% annual growth, on average over several years given lumpiness. Capex is INR30-35 crore for FY27 and INR50-60 crore for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is AF Holdings exiting, and what is the O&M run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the PE investor exited because its fund had a limited life and referred the question to them. On O&M, it said some contracts start in H2 and billing is milestone-based, with an O&M EBITDA margin in the low 20s%.

risks_watch: Gulf logistics: sea freight from UAE remains uncertain and costlier, which could delay Q3/Q4 deliveries and the expected H2 revenue ramp.
Margin recovery depends on a low double-digit FY27 EBITDA; Q1 EBITDA was reported as negative 18%, and fixed costs remain high.
Order conversion: the pipeline is about INR3,000 crore at 15-20% conversion, so guided intake of INR500-600 crore must come through.
Working capital at 140-150 days, with bank non-fund-based limits needed for guarantees and LCs.
Forex exposure from the Mexican peso against the dollar.
Sharjah investment decision in Q4 FY27 and its effect on capex; CBG feedstock constraints and municipal waste policy changes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium term and on H2 execution, but cautious on the near term: management repeatedly tied margin recovery to FY28 and flagged Gulf logistics as an ongoing risk. Some answers were deferred to follow-up (data centre water metrics, ZLD market share), and the management gave the 20-25% growth target "cautiously".
